<Rep. Maxine Waters, Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, Rep. Al Green, Rep. Brad Sherman, Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, Rep. Bill Foster, Rep. Juan Vargas, Rep. Ayanna Pressley, Rep. Nikema Williams, Rep. Joyce Beatty, Rep. Sean Casten, Rep. Sylvia R. Garcia>: alternative trading systems from listing or otherwise
trading digital assets issued by the President, Vice
President, and public officials (including Members of
Congress).
• Rep. Liccardo's amendment (#2) requires the
DeFi study in the ``CALAMITY Act'' bill to look at the
feasibility to de-anonymize users of a sandboxed DeFi
system through a court order.
• Rep. Gonzalez's amendment directs the
Treasury to review the use of digital assets by
transnational criminal organizations and foreign
terrorist organizations and provide input to Congress,
financial institutions, and the SEC and CFTC.
• Rep. Foster's amendment (#1) requires the
federal financial regulators to conduct a study on the
application of digital identity credentials in the
blockchain ecosystem, with emphasis on the technology's
ability to facilitate Bank Secrecy Act compliance,
preserve privacy, and promote market integrity.
The CALAMITY Act passed out of Committee, with a final vote of 32-19.\49\ The Committee previously approved a different version of this bill last Congress\50\ on a 35-15 vote and later passed out of the House on a 279-136 vote.\51\
\49\House Committee on Financial Services, Committee Markup, 119th Cong. (June 10, 2025).
\50\House Committee on Financial Services, Committee Markup, 118th Cong. (Jul. 26, 2023).
\51\House Vote on H.R. 4763 (May 22, 2024) (279 yeas, 136 nays).
Finally, this bill is opposed by the following groups: Accountable.US/Accountable.NOW, American Association for Justice, Americans for Financial Reform, Center for American Progress, Center for Responsible Lending, Chastity Murphy (Visiting Research Fellow, University of Manchester Law and Technology Initiative), Consumer Federation of America, Consumer Reports, Demand Progress, Democracy Defenders Action, Hilary Allen (Professor of Law, American University Washington College of Law), Lee Reiners (Lecturing Fellow, Duke University), National Consumer Law Center on behalf of its low-income clients, North American Securities Administrators Association, Office of the Attorney General of the State of New York, Public Citizen, Raul Carrillo (Kellis E. Parker Teaching Fellow, Academic Fellow, Lecturer in Law, Columbia Law School), Revolving Door Project, Richard Painter (S. Walter Richey Professor of Corporate Law, University of Minnesota Law School; White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush), Rohan Grey (Assistant Professor of Law, Willamette University College of Law).
For these reasons, we oppose H.R. 3633.
Sincerely,
Maxine Waters,
Ranking Member.
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Al Green,
Brad Sherman,
Emanuel Cleaver, II,
Bill Foster,
Juan Vargas,
Ayanna Pressley,
Nikema Williams,
Joyce Beatty,
Sean Casten,
Sylvia R. Garcia,
Members of Congress.
